record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: For distributed differential privacy in federated learning, what are the optimal privacy, accuracy, and communication trade-offs for secure shuffling, secure aggregation, and finite-precision privatization schemes, including lower bounds and matching upper bounds under fixed communication budgets?

evidence.quote: optimal communication, privacy, and accuracy tradeoffs

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a distributed estimation/learning setting with $n$ clients, each holding a local datum $x_i$ from a domain $\mathcal{X}$ (e.g., a vector in the unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^d$, or a sample from a distribution). A central server wishes to compute a statistic $f(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ (for example, the mean) while providing $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differential privacy on the joint output with respect to changing any single $x_i$. Each client may apply a local randomizer $R_i$ producing a message of at most $b$ bits (a fixed per-client communication budget). Consider the following three distributed privacy architectures:

1. Secure shuffling: each client sends $R_i(x_i)$ to a trusted shuffler that outputs a uniformly random permutation of the messages; the server sees only the shuffled multiset.
2. Secure aggregation: clients use a cryptographic protocol so that the server learns only $\sum_i R_i(x_i)$ (modulo some group), each summand being a finite-precision privatized contribution.
3. Finite-precision (quantized) privatization: each client outputs a discrete-valued privatized message of at most $b$ bits, without shuffling or aggregation.

For each of these three architectures, and for canonical estimation tasks (e.g., $d$-dimensional mean estimation in $\ell_2$ or $\ell_\infty$, frequency estimation over a finite alphabet, and stochastic convex optimization), determine the optimal trade-off between:
- the differential-privacy parameters $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ at the server's view,
- the worst-case estimation error (e.g., mean-squared error) over the data class, and
- the per-client communication budget $b$ in bits.

Specifically, establish matching information-theoretic lower bounds and achievable upper bounds (up to constants) on the minimax error as a function of $(n,d,\varepsilon,\delta,b)$ for each of the three architectures, including the regime $b = O(1)$ and the regime of small $\varepsilon$.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on individual instances of these trade-offs: matching upper and lower bounds are known for mean estimation under communication and privacy constraints in the shuffle model (e.g., Girgis et al. 2020), and tight bounds exist for $\ell_2$ mean estimation under streaming DP. However, a comprehensive set of matching bounds covering all three architectures (shuffling, secure aggregation, finite-precision local DP) across canonical tasks and parameter regimes remains incomplete, with ongoing work refining bounds and broadening assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Shuffled Model of Federated Learning: Privacy, Communication and Accuracy Trade-offs
status_evidence.snippet: Provides upper and lower bounds for mean estimation with privacy and communication constraints in the shuffle model.
status_evidence.claim: Matching bounds known in specific shuffle-model mean estimation settings.

status_evidence.title: Improved communication-privacy trade-offs in L2 mean estimation under streaming DP
status_evidence.snippet: Improved trade-offs for L2 mean estimation under privacy and communication constraints.
status_evidence.claim: Tight trade-offs continue to be improved, indicating the general problem is not fully closed.

status_evidence.title: Analysis of Shuffling Beyond Pure Local Differential Privacy
status_evidence.snippet: New asymptotic privacy analysis for shuffled local randomizers beyond pure LDP.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research suggests the broader problem remains open.
